topics.topic: Handling service request body-read or decode failure after framing acceptance
questions: If the listener accepted the framing headers but the service API cannot finish reading or decoding the request body, does it call `operations`, which failure wins over an invalid token or other stage-(1) failure, and what answer is produced?
When accepted framing is followed by a body-stream failure, who handles it, what failure reaches the service, and is the connection closed?

When the framing headers were accepted but the service API cannot finish reading or decoding the request body, does it still call `operations`, with what representation of the failed or partially read request, and which module produces the failure answer?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P2 about handing an unreadable service request to operations, applying stage (1) first, and returning the later wire-format refusal; the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Which operations-stage failure results from an unreadable service-request body and whether later stages are invoked
quotes:
Nothing is reachable without a token; every request goes to
`operations.perform_service_operation`; it checks nothing and holds no rule
(State 3). Not served in an owner-only start (A17 rule 1).

None of its own: it refuses nothing. An operation name that is not one of
A09 rule 2's reaches `operations`, which refuses it at stage (1) as outside
the service's rights (`not_permitted`, `outside_service_rights`), whatever
token it carries once the token is valid; inputs that are not of the wire
format — a body that cannot be read as it, a field it does not declare, a
value of another shape than its field's — are answered stage (1) first and
then `invalid_request` (`outside_closed_list`) at stage (4). A declared
field left out is not a wire-format failure: it reaches the operation as
absent, and its module answers it (`missing_value`, A02). Every refusal is
`operations`'.
precedent.why: State 5 says an unreadable service body reaches `operations.perform_service_operation`, undergoes stage (1), and is then refused at stage (4) as `invalid_request` with `outside_closed_list`, rather than being treated as merely absent declared fields.

topics.topic: Handling upload file-stream failure after head admission
questions: After a valid upload head has admitted the owner request and the file part's stream then fails, which module capability detects and reports the unreadable file, who calls it, and how is that refusal returned while preserving the previously kept upload?

After an upload head has passed the owner-session and CSRF checks, which module capability reads the file stream, which failure does a later stream error produce, how is it rendered, and when is the connection closed?

After an upload head has been admitted, which module capability reads the file-part stream, which caller invokes it, and what exact failure does it return if the stream becomes unreadable before the file is complete?

judgement.why: This asks the same ownership and orchestration question as P3 for the unread upload stream, migration_import's file_unreadable refusal, rendering, preservation of the kept upload, and connection closure; the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: State 3 ownership and capability orchestration for reading owner requests, importing file streams, rendering failures, and closing connections
quotes:
`module:owner_interface`. The owner interface: server-rendered, script-free
forms over the owner's operations (R0-29, A19).
`boundary:owner_browser`, `module:instance_lifecycle`.

One HTTP request from the owner's browser: the session cookie, the form's
fields with their CSRF value, a confirmation value where the step carries
one, the revision or access version the rendered card carried; for an
upload, a multipart body whose first part is the CSRF field and whose second
is the file (owner, 2026-11-17). `upload_framing.read_upload_head` reads
the body's head alone and answers the CSRF value and the file part's
declared length; `owner_interface` hands that length and the file part, as
an unread stream that ends where the part ends, to
`operations.perform_owner_operation`, without reading or buffering it.

After an upload's answer, whatever it was — accepted, or refused before any
or after some bytes were read — `owner_interface` discards the unread
remainder of the body without reading it into anything and closes the
connection its listener accepted; a connection that carried an upload is
never reused.

`module:upload_framing`. Read an upload's multipart head alone, so that its
CSRF value travels in the form and the file reaches `migration_import`
unread (A13 rules 5, 7; owner, 2026-11-17).
`module:owner_interface`.

The file part's stream is a `MultipartFileBody`, the class
`upload_framing` owns that implements `UploadBody` (State 6); it fails
when the request's stream ends before the closing delimiter, which
`migration_import.read_import_mapping` refuses as `file_unreadable`, as any
stream that fails.
precedent.why: State 5 names `serve_owner_request`'s owner and caller and assigns upload-head reading, the handoff through operations, refusal rendering, unread-body disposal, and connection closure.

When an ordinary owner form cannot be completely read or decoded, what values are handed to `operations`, what failure is returned, and how is A13's required session admission and idle-time restart performed?

judgement.divergence: One implementer discards all partially decoded form fields and hands operations no CSRF value, producing the stage-(1) CSRF refusal; another retains a completely decoded valid CSRF value and hands the remaining field as absent, producing the applicable later-stage missing-value refusal. The owner sees different refusal pages, although A13 requires both requests to refresh the session's idle time.
judgement.why: The texts require an accepted-framing owner request to reach operations and refresh a valid session, but do not say whether successfully decoded fields survive a later ordinary-form body failure or how that failure is represented to operations.

witness.initial: A valid owner session is near its idle limit, and an owner correction form has accepted framing; its valid CSRF field is completely read before the body stream fails ahead of a required value.
events: The owner submits the correction with the valid session cookie and CSRF value.
The owner interface reads the CSRF field, then encounters the body-stream failure before reading a required correction value.
The owner interface hands the request representation to operations, which admits the valid session and applies the ordered checks.
outcomes: The owner interface discards the partially decoded fields, so operations receives no CSRF value and returns the stage-(1) CSRF refusal.
The owner interface retains the decoded CSRF value and represents the unread required value as absent, so operations passes stage (1) and returns the applicable missing-value refusal at stage (4).
witness.observer: The owner sees different refusal pages; in both cases the request refreshes the valid session as A13 requires.
basis:
Every request of a caller whose framing headers the listener accepted
(`instance_lifecycle`) enters through one of the two surfaces, which decide
nothing ("Explicit exclusions", R0-29): the service API reads the token and the
request and hands them to `operations`; the owner interface reads the cookie,
the CSRF value and the form and hands them to `operations`, and renders its
answer as escaped text (A19 rules 1, 2).

An owner
   request is any request to the owner interface that
   carries the valid session, whatever its answer; its arrival restarts the 30
   minutes — of concurrent requests the latest arrival counts; before the
   first request it runs from the sign-in.

Every change carries CSRF protection and
is validated on the server; a change made against an older revision is refused
(R0-35).

topics.topic: Upload head completion boundary, owner-session admission, and operations handoff
questions: If the listener accepted the framing headers but the upload head ends early, exceeds its head bound, has malformed multipart framing, or otherwise cannot be read, which module produces which refusal, and is the request considered to have arrived for owner-session admission?
Does the owner interface hand an upload to `operations` immediately after reading its head so the session check occurs before the file is streamed, or only after it has read the entire form?

If the upload's multipart head or its stream fails before the head has been completely read, which module and capability handle that pre-arrival failure, what answer is produced, and is any partially read CSRF value used or discarded?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P7 about upload-head read failures, the absence of returned head values, stage-(1) refusal, and the distinction between a head failure and a later file-stream failure; the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Which body failures are covered by the phrase “reading fails”
quotes:
inputs that are not of the wire
format — a body that cannot be read as it, a field it does not declare, a
value of another shape than its field's — are answered stage (1) first and
then `invalid_request` (`outside_closed_list`) at stage (4).

The CSRF value the first part carries, the delimiter that ends the file
part, and the file part's declared length — the request's declared length
less the head it read and the closing delimiter with its final `--` and line
end, or none when the request declared none; or that the head is not of that form — no multipart content type or
boundary, a first part that is not the CSRF field, no second part that is
the file — or is longer than the imported `UPLOAD_FORM_HEAD_MAX_BYTES`
constant, or declares less than that head and the closing delimiter, or the
request's stream fails or ends while the head is read — with none of these
values.

None: a head of another form answers no CSRF value, and the upload is
refused at stage (1) as a change without one (A04 rule 6, A13 rule 5).
precedent.why: State 5 distinguishes decoding or parsing a complete but malformed request, which produces a refusal, from a stream failure while reading the body or upload head.

topics.topic: Registry response attempt and connection disposition after body-reader failure
questions: After a surface or upload reader reports a body-stream failure, must Registry attempt to send the refusal, and must it close the connection or may it reuse the connection when the framing boundary is still known?
After any surface's body reader receives this failure, does Registry attempt to send the operation's refusal, and must it close the connection or may it keep the connection alive?

judgement.why: This asks the same question as P1 about which surface produces the response after a body-read failure and the resulting connection closure; the relevant texts have not changed.

precedent.topic: Which module and capability attempt the failure response and close the connection after a body-read failure
quotes:
`module:service_api`. The service API's transport for the four services
(R0-27, R0-28).

One response in that wire format, v1's (owner, 2026-11-17): the answer, or
the refusal's code, stage and kinds.

`module:owner_interface`. The owner interface: server-rendered, script-free
forms over the owner's operations (R0-29, A19).

One HTML page: the answer rendered, every stored value escaped as text for
its place, under a content security policy forbidding any script; or the
refusal rendered — the sign-in page for a request without a valid session.

After an upload's answer, whatever it was — accepted, or refused before any
or after some bytes were read — `owner_interface` discards the unread
remainder of the body without reading it into anything and closes the
connection its listener accepted; a connection that carried an upload is
never reused.
precedent.why: State 5 assigns response production to the two surface capabilities and explicitly assigns upload-response cleanup and connection closure to `owner_interface.serve_owner_request`.
